findings.title: Flex container ignores the small-action button's float, losing right alignment
findings.body: Making `.small-action` a flex container turns its direct children into flex items. The existing `button { float: right; }` at line 309 is therefore ignored, and the button has no auto margin or other flex rule that allocates the remaining space. The action/undo button will render immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge of the row. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button or otherwise distribute the free space explicitly.

findings.title: Legacy order properties need +1 to match standard order semantics
findings.body: The new `order($val)` mixin passes the standard zero-based `order` value directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. Those legacy flexbox properties are one-based and default to 1, while modern `order` defaults to 0. Calls such as `order(0)` or `order(1)` will place items differently in the old `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` fallback than in modern flex. Emit `$val + 1` for the legacy properties while keeping `$val` for `-ms-flex-order`, `-webkit-order`, and `order`. The current 2/3 calls happen to preserve their relative order, but the reusable mixin is incorrect for common values.

findings.title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align and emits an invalid -ms property
findings.body: `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, but `align-items()` never emits the corresponding `-moz-box-align`; it also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real CSS property. In an old Firefox that falls back to `-moz-box`, requested alignment (`center` in the header and `.small-action`, `baseline` in badges) will not apply, and the non-existent `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead code. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` and remove `-ms-align-items`.
